title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page image is upside down. It is a typed page numbered '- 22 -' from a text on the cohomology of ringed sites. It does not continue the handwritten notes on abelian varieties and Gysin maps on the neighbouring pages. Most likely it is a typescript sheet, perhaps by a student or collaborator, reused or filed in the folder. Its content is the standard characterization of sheaves that are acyclic on every object of a site.

Setting: C is a ringed site and G a sheaf of A-modules. ℋ^0(G) denotes G viewed as a presheaf on C°. ℋ^q(G) is the presheaf X ↦ H^q(X,G). The Čech presheaves are Ȟ^q ℋ^0(G).

Proposition 3.1: the following conditions are equivalent.
(i) For every object X and every covering sieve R ↪ X, H^q(C°/R, ℋ^0 G) = 0 for all q > 0. This is the cohomology of the presheaf on the sieve, i.e. Ext^q(Z_R, G) in presheaves.
(ii) For every X, Ȟ^q(X, G) = 0 for q > 0.
(ii)bis The presheaves Ȟ^q ℋ^0(G) vanish for q > 0.
(iii) For every X, H^q(X, G) = 0 for q > 0.
(iii)bis The presheaves ℋ^q(G) vanish for q > 0.

Proof as given:
- (ii)⇔(ii)bis and (iii)⇔(iii)bis hold by definition.
- (i)⇒(ii) holds because Čech cohomology is the colimit over covering sieves of H^q(R, ℋ^0 G).
- (iii)bis⇒(i) follows from the spectral sequence H^p(C°/R, ℋ^q G) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X, G) of Prop. 2.3. Here one uses that Z_R → Z_X becomes an isomorphism after sheafification.
- (ii)bis⇒(iii)bis is Cartan's induction, using Ȟ^0 ℋ^q(G) = 0 for q > 0 (the 'last assertion of (2.5)').

Definition 3.2 calls such G 'C-acyclic'. This is exactly SGA 4 V, Prop. 4.3 (the 'flasque' / Cartan criterion), in a presentation with sieves.
errors: No mathematical error. The proof sketch is complete modulo the cited earlier results (formulas (12), (14), (15), Prop. 2.3 and (2.5)), which are standard.

ideas.what: Equivalence of sieve-cohomology vanishing, Čech vanishing and derived-cohomology vanishing on all objects of a site; such sheaves are called C-acyclic
ideas.modern_name: Cartan's criterion / flasque (Čech-acyclic) sheaves on a site
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (topological case); Grothendieck–Verdier, SGA 4 Exp. V (sites)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé V, §4 (Prop. 4.3, flasque sheaves); cf. Tôhoku for Čech spectral sequences

ideas.what: Spectral sequence relating presheaf cohomology on a covering sieve to sheaf cohomology
